challenge.method: Tested whether SPDX’s extra opening Netscape title, the embedded Mozilla title, the negative cross-reference match, or the §13 substitution defeated the correspondence. Compared the express composition paragraphs, amendment V.3, both notices, and the exact license-choice phrase.
challenge.results: The publisher begins with “AMENDMENTS.” SPDX adds “Netscape Public LIcense version 1.1” before that heading. Both then identify NPL 1.1 in the composition paragraph and Netscape exhibit. Both include the later Mozilla heading and exhibit. The §13 substitution defeats verbatim correspondence and prevents an inference of interchangeable terms. It does not displace either document’s express identification of the combined edition.

limitations: Publisher §13 says “Your choice of the NPL or the alternative licenses.” SPDX licenseText says “Your choice of the MPL or the alternative licenses.” The difference changes the named license in the clause.
SPDX records crossRef.match as the string “false” for its Mozilla page URL. That field supplies no positive text-match evidence for the pinned plaintext.
The crosswalk supports lookup by named edition. Legal equivalence, selection of governing wording, and application to a particular work remain undetermined.
